title: Avoid per-packet UDP Vec allocation in Rust WebRTC receive loop
description:
Context: The Rust WebRTC sidecar copies every inbound UDP datagram into a fresh Vec before handing it from the UDP reader task to the main RTC loop. Evidence: server/webrtc-rs/src/webrtc_session.rs:126 allocates the reusable recv buffer, but server/webrtc-rs/src/webrtc_session.rs:148 does buf[..len].to_vec() for every packet. On an active WebRTC session this is on the STUN/DTLS/SRTP hot path.

Goal: Remove or amortize this allocation/copy. Prefer keeping UDP input processing in the owner loop if feasible, or introduce a bounded packet buffer/pool/Bytes-style ownership that avoids one heap allocation per received packet. Cache local_udp_addr instead of calling local_addr() per packet while touching this code.

Acceptance criteria:
- Inbound UDP handling no longer does Vec::to_vec()/fresh heap allocation per datagram on the steady-state hot path.
- Ownership/lifetime remains compatible with str0m Receive::new and rtc.handle_input.
- Packet handling remains bounded/backpressure-aware; avoid unbounded queue growth.
- Add a small host test or documented measurement/trace showing the allocation site is gone.

Baseline checked from branch mjc/webrtc-hotpath-allocation-audit: nix develop --command cargo test --manifest-path server/webrtc-rs/Cargo.toml passes.

title: Cache screen settings instead of allocating file reads every H264 frame
description:
Context: capture_frame calls Screen::read() once per scheduled H.264 frame at server/webrtc-rs/src/webrtc_session.rs:310. Screen::read() then reads /kvmapp/kvm/res, /kvmapp/kvm/fps, and /kvmapp/kvm/qlty with fs::read_to_string at server/webrtc-rs/src/screen.rs:14-17 and 35-40. At 30-60 fps this means repeated file opens plus String allocations before every KVM capture.

Goal: Move screen configuration out of the per-frame hot path. Cache the parsed Screen in CaptureState or a small watcher/poller, and refresh only when needed using a lower-frequency interval, mtime check, or explicit config-change path.

Acceptance criteria:
- Steady-state frame capture does not call fs::read_to_string for res/fps/qlty every frame.
- FPS/bitrate/resolution changes are still picked up within a documented bounded delay.
- Frame scheduling uses a stable frame duration until a refreshed setting changes it.
- Add tests for validation/defaulting and for refresh behavior if the cache logic is pure enough to test on host.

Baseline checked from branch mjc/webrtc-hotpath-allocation-audit: nix develop --command cargo test --manifest-path server/webrtc-rs/Cargo.toml passes.

title: Make H264 diagnostic logging allocation-light
description:
Context: describe_h264 is called for the first 16 frames, every 120th frame, and any result == 3 from capture_frame. It allocates a Vec<String> of formatted bytes and joins it at server/webrtc-rs/src/webrtc_session.rs:506-512, then annex_b_nal_types allocates a Vec<u8> at server/webrtc-rs/src/webrtc_session.rs:521-528. This is throttled, so it is lower priority than the steady-state UDP/frame allocations, but result == 3 may make it more frequent depending on libkvm semantics.

Goal: Keep the useful diagnostic output while avoiding avoidable heap churn. Consider writing into a stack-backed ArrayString/SmallVec, formatting directly into the tracing field/string, or returning a fixed-size NAL summary array/count. Also confirm whether result == 3 should log every such frame.

Acceptance criteria:
- describe_h264 no longer allocates Vec<String> for the hex prefix.
- NAL type summary avoids heap allocation or documents why allocation is acceptable.
- Log throttling is reviewed so normal successful streaming cannot accidentally log/allocate every frame.
- Existing H264 description tests continue to pass or are updated to cover the new representation.

title: Reduce H264 frame copy between libkvm and str0m writer
description:
Context: KvmApi::read_h264 copies the libkvm-owned H.264 frame into a new Vec at server/webrtc-rs/src/kvm.rs:184, frees the original C buffer, then capture_frame moves that Vec into str0m writer.write at server/webrtc-rs/src/webrtc_session.rs:380-382. This may be the safest ownership boundary today, but it means at least one heap allocation and full frame copy for every encoded frame. KvmWorker::read_h264 also creates a fresh reply channel per frame at server/webrtc-rs/src/kvm.rs:104.

Goal: Investigate and, if safe with libkvm ownership rules, reduce per-frame allocation/copy overhead. Options include a reusable frame buffer, an owned wrapper that frees via free_kvmv_data on Drop if str0m can consume/clone appropriately, or a worker API that reuses a response path instead of allocating a oneshot std channel per frame.

Acceptance criteria:
- Document libkvm buffer ownership constraints and why the chosen approach is safe.
- Reduce or justify the per-frame to_vec copy with measurement from device-sized frames.
- Avoid leaks/double-free on negative result, zero-size result, writer errors, and dropped sessions.
- Keep the existing read/free lifecycle tests or add targeted coverage/mocks for the new ownership path.

title: Rust WebRTC sidecar MVP
description: Track the NanoKVM Rust WebRTC sidecar rollout and the evidence needed before it can replace the legacy Go/Pion endpoint by default. The browser contract stays /api/stream/h264; Go remains the authenticated public HTTP/WebSocket boundary; Rust owns WebRTC/media/hardware capture on the rust backend.
design: Test scope is split into host-build, Go boundary, Rust signaling, Rust WebRTC/RTP, hardware capture, packaging/startup, on-device behavior, rollback, and regression suites. Each child issue names the thing under test, the concrete setup, expected observations, and likely failure signals. Keep tests reproducible through nix develop where possible; device-only checks should record exact NanoKVM firmware/library provenance and logs under /data.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every sidecar subsystem has at least one Beads issue with Thing under test, Setup, Assertions, Failure signals, and Evidence to capture.
- Host-side tests cover cargo/go/nix build regressions without NanoKVM hardware.
- Device-side tests cover successful video, reconnect, process isolation from Go/Pion/kvm_system, and rollback.
- Known risky boundaries are explicit: libkvm ABI, hardware prep, H.264 frame shape, ICE/DTLS/SRTP negotiation, and service boot ordering.
notes: Known good manual result: Rust sidecar built from branch ran on NanoKVM at 192.168.1.6 from /data/nanokvm-test/nanokvm-webrtc-rs against /kvmapp/server/dl_lib copied into /data/nanokvm-test/dl_lib, listened on 0.0.0.0:6040, initialized KVM vision, and produced browser video. Do not treat repo-local dl_lib as the known-good runtime set for device validation unless packaging intentionally updates the device libraries.

title: Test: H.264 frame handling and RTP emission
description: Test Rust handling of H.264 frames from libkvm through str0m RTP emission.
design: Thing under test: Annex-B frame classification, SPS/PPS/I-frame preservation, P-frame handling, media timestamp increments, playout-delay extension, payload type selection, RTP writer behavior. Setup: host tests with synthetic Annex-B samples and device/browser test with real frames. Assertions: first keyframe includes SPS/PPS before IDR; P-frames are sent after keyframe; MediaTime increments by Screen::frame_duration; negotiated H264 PT is used; frame.data empty never writes RTP; RTCP input does not block transmit. Failure signals: black screen despite positive frame bytes, missing SPS/PPS, wrong PT, nonmonotonic timestamps, repeated first-frame decode failure, or writer missing after connection.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests cover Annex-B NAL detection for SPS/PPS/IDR/P frames.
- Integration log proves negotiated H264 PT and frames_sent increments.
- Browser webrtc-internals shows inbound-rtp bytesReceived and framesDecoded increasing.
- Packet capture or str0m log confirms RTP timestamp progression at configured FPS.
- Empty/error capture result is dropped without RTP write.
notes: Useful evidence: Rust logs around H264 frame read/queued, chrome://webrtc-internals dump, and a short tcpdump/pcap if available.

Do not start legacy Go/Pion/kvm_system unless this test explicitly says it is a legacy or rollback case.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass/fail result is explicit for the named thing under test.
Setup is reproducible from a clean checkout or documented /data device directory.
Logs or command output distinguish capture, signaling, RTP, browser decode, and boot-mode failures.
Any failure produces either a follow-up bug or an update to the parent sidecar MVP issue.
notes: Part of the expanded Rust WebRTC sidecar test matrix. Keep bulky raw logs out of git; summarize results in Beads and store temporary device artifacts under /data when needed.

title: Test: S95 invalid mode fallback
description:
Thing under test: unexpected /data/go-app-boot contents

Setup: write unsupported value then start service

Assertions: fallback behavior is deterministic and documented

Failure signals: mixed process set, silent bad state

Evidence to capture: file content and ps output

description:
Thing under test: service stop cleanup

Setup: start each mode then stop

Assertions: all NanoKVM/Rust/kvm_system processes for that mode are gone

Failure signals: stale process, port still bound

Evidence to capture: ps and ss output
